goldens.comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
goldens.reasoning: C5 mentions indexOf, but it is about parse errors, not case sensitivity.

goldens.comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
goldens.reasoning: None of the candidates raise the race condition in backup code use.

goldens.comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
goldens.reasoning: C2 identifies the same leak: the object URL is not revoked on close/reset.

candidates: Component is exported as `function TwoFactor` even though it's a backup-code UI; the name mismatch can be confusing in stack traces/DevTools and when importing alongside the real `TwoFactor` component

A new object URL is created for `backupCodesUrl`, but it's only revoked when generating a new one; if the modal is closed/reset without another setup run, the object URL can leak and keep the blob alive longer than intended
`navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` isn't awaited/handled, so the success toast can show even if the clipboard write fails (e.g., permissions/unsupported environment)

Renders an `<a>` wrapping a `Button` that becomes a `<button>`, which creates nested interactive elements (`<a><button>…`). This can cause inconsistent click/keyboard behavior and is invalid HTML semantics

`JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` can throw (or return a non-array) if `backupCodes` is corrupted/unexpected, which would crash the authorize/disable flow with a 500. Consider guarding parse/decrypt errors and validating the decoded shape before using `indexOf`
